declared_exclusions.item: Deliverable 4 -- the DNS cutover and the ACM certificate for opalinvest.com.
declared_exclusions.reason: NOT EXECUTABLE FROM THIS FABRIC, not deferred by choice. opalinvest.com has no Route53 hosted zone (denominator 2 zones, IsTruncated absent) and is delegated to GoDaddy ns47/ns48.domaincontrol.com, read authoritatively from GoDaddy's own nameserver. No ACM certificate for the name exists (us-east-1 denominator 1, opalinvest.dev only) and minting one requires a validation CNAME in that same GoDaddy zone, so the certificate and the cutover are blocked by ONE credential. A second independent carrier agrees: infra/aws/terraform/website/README.md calls the EIP 'the stable public IP handed to GoDaddy apex-A at W3 cutover'. Separately, the apex is an A record and CloudFront publishes no stable IP, and RFC 1034 s.3.6.2 forbids a CNAME at a zone apex -- so an ALIAS-class record is needed, which Route53 provides and whose GoDaddy equivalent is NOT ESTABLISHED here. Row NFRA_OPSEC202609-Z-S101, ARMED.

declared_exclusions.item: Graduating any managed rule group from Count to Block.
declared_exclusions.reason: Explicitly a later act on measured soak evidence shared with the portal's, per the face and the S-4-18 carrier. A group in Block here would enforce an unmeasured ruleset on live visitor traffic in front of a public marketing site and is a FAIL under S13-AC4, not a bonus. AWSManagedRulesBotControlRuleSet is unauthorized under PRD s.5 and is deliberately absent.

sg-062bbb40a6c92509c permits tcp/80 and tcp/443 from 0.0.0.0/0 and the EIP answers on both, so the origin serves non-edge traffic today and the edge is bypassable by requesting the address directly. S13-AC5 requires the security group to be IDENTICAL before and after, so closing it is explicitly NOT this face's act. Named here so that no claim in this instance is read as 'known-bad requests are refused' without its scope -- any refusal this face demonstrates is scoped to traffic that traversed the edge.

The distribution runs Managed-CachingDisabled. The cell's outcome is a SECURITY one -- a known-bad request refused before WordPress handles it -- not a performance one, and caching a logged-in WordPress response to the wrong viewer is a correctness and privacy defect. A WP-appropriate cookie/query-string cache policy is a separate, measured act.
